== Changes in working tree (what needs to ship)

=== 1. `fix(darwin): ssh-keys activation chain` (three fixes bundled)

These resolve activation-chain gaps uncovered by the bioskop switch.

==== 1a. `modules/darwin/linux-builder.nix` — nix-store-identity via postActivation

`nix-store-identity-deploy` was wired as a custom-named
`system.activationScripts.nixStoreIdentity`, which **nix-darwin silently drops**
(only well-known phase names get emitted into the activate script). Moved into
`system.activationScripts.postActivation.text = lib.mkOrder 1600 ''...''`,
ordered after `ssh-keys-enrichment.postActivation` (mkOrder 1500) so
`/var/lib/ndh/ssh-keys/nix-store{,-cert.pub}` exists before deploy copies it to
`/etc/nix/`.

==== 1b. `modules/darwin/ssh-keys-enrichment.nix` — `sudo -H` for user-context steps

macOS `sudo -u <user>` preserves root's `$HOME=/var/root`, so
`install -d -m 700 ~/.ssh` in `ssh-ensure-authorized-keys` failed with
"cannot create directory '/var/root'". Added `-H` to both
`launchctl asuser … sudo -u <user>` invocations
(`ssh-extract-keys-user` and `ssh-ensure-authorized-keys`).

==== 1c. `modules/home-manager/default.nix` — HM materializer gate fix (disk-image-in-switch closure)

Every `darwin-rebuild switch` was dragging the nixos bringup disk image
derivation into the activation-script closure, even though
`hosts/bioskop/default.nix:9` sets
`vmMaterializerEnableActivationHook = false`.

Root cause: the existing gate in HM `default.nix` was:

[source,nix]
----
hostVmMaterializerActivationHook = lib.attrByPath
  [ "host" "vmMaterializerEnableActivationHook" ] true resolvedProfile;
----

The `profile.host` submodule in `profile.nix` **does not declare**
`vmMaterializerEnableActivationHook`, so the module system filters it out.
`nix eval .#darwinConfigurations.bioskop.config.profile.host` returns only
`{form, hostAlias, hostName, nixosBringupRootFs}` — the value from
`hosts/bioskop/default.nix:9` never reaches `resolvedProfile`.

The canonical option `config.vmMaterializer.enableActivationHook` exists in
`modules/.common.d/vm-materializer.nix:20` but it's not visible from HM's
`config` (HM `config` is the user-scope config, not nix-darwin top-level).

**Fix**: read the raw value from
`specialArgs.ndh.context.hostProfile.vmMaterializerEnableActivationHook`
— same path the canonical option uses, but without the submodule stripping.

[source,nix]
----
hostVmMaterializerActivationHook =
  if ndhContext != null && ndhContext ? hostProfile && ndhContext.hostProfile != null then
    ndhContext.hostProfile.vmMaterializerEnableActivationHook or true
  else
    true;
----

Verified: `home-manager.users.nxmatic.home.activation.materializeVm` is
ABSENT on bioskop after the fix; `nix-instantiate` shows zero
`bioskop-zfs-disk-images-raw` references in the toplevel closure.

=== 2. `refactor(keys): profile name "host" → "system"`

Operator-requested rename: "host" was ambiguous (collided with
`profile.host` submodule, `ssh-host` cert type, hostname, etc.). The
profile-role axis is really about **where extracted key material lands**,
so "system" is clearer.

Scope:

* `modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.schema.yaml` — enum `host` → `system`;
  expanded `profileName` description to spell out placement:
** `bringup` — bundled into the nixos minimal bringup image.
** `system` — root-owned host-wide paths (`sshPaths.systemKeysDir`,
   i.e. `/var/lib/ndh/ssh-keys/` on darwin, plus downstream copies to
   `/etc/nix/`, sshd HostKey, etc.).
** `user` — per-operator paths under
   `~/.local/var/run/secrets/ssh-keys/`.
* `profile.nix` — enum + default list + docstring.
* `hosts/nikopol/profile.nix` — `profile.names = lib.mkForce ["system" "user"]`.
* `modules/darwin/ssh-keys-enrichment.nix` — profileNames fallback default.
* `modules/nixos/systemd/ssh-keys-enrichment.nix` — profileNames fallback default + two comments.
* `modules/home-manager/ssh-key.d/ssh-extract-keys.split-exp.yq` —
  the `[ "host" ] - $profiles` membership test becomes `[ "system" ] - $profiles`.
* `modules/.common.d/ssh-keys.d/ssh-split-keys-yaml.sh` — "Host scope" comment +
  yq filter `== "host"` → `== "system"`.
* `modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml` (sops) — 4 keys rewritten via
  `sops set` per-element (sops 3.12.1 only accepts scalars for `set`,
  not arrays):

[source,sh]
----
# nix-store: [bringup, host] → [bringup, system]  (index 1)
sops set modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml \
  '["keys"]["nix-store"]["profiles"][1]' '"system"'
# linux-builder: [host] → [system]  (index 0)
sops set modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml \
  '["keys"]["linux-builder"]["profiles"][0]' '"system"'
# rdp-host: [host, user] → [system, user]  (index 0)
sops set modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml \
  '["keys"]["rdp-host"]["profiles"][0]' '"system"'
# vz-guest-nixos: [host] → [system]  (index 0)
sops set modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml \
  '["keys"]["vz-guest-nixos"]["profiles"][0]' '"system"'
----

`# sops:encrypted` markers preserved (7 before, 7 after — verified via grep).

==== What's NOT renamed (deliberately)

* `profile.host.*` submodule (host-form axis — hostname/alias/vmProvider/form
  — completely different from the profile-role axis).
* `ssh-host` / `ssh-user` `cert_usage` tags — those are OpenSSH cert types,
  not profile names.
* `principalsYamlLabel = "host"` in `modules/darwin/openssh.nix:44` — an
  inert yq-recursion wrapper label.

=== 3. `refactor(keys-validator): drop shadow file, validate canonical`

* Deleted `modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.v2.yaml` (memory note: "shadow
  file, redundant with canonical `keys.yaml`").
* `flake.nix` `ssh-keys-v2-validate` app: now defaults to the canonical
  `modules/home-manager/ssh.d/keys.yaml`, sops-decrypts into a mktemp
  tempfile (cleanup via `trap EXIT`), runs `check-jsonschema` on the
  plaintext. Falls back to verbatim copy if decrypt fails (lets you still
  validate an already-decrypted sample).

`nix run .#ssh-keys-v2-validate` → `ok -- validation done`.

== Known open issues (carry-forward)

=== `nerdNixosBuilderKey` silently dropped on darwin

`modules/darwin/linux-builder.nix:286` wires the linux-builder private
deploy via `system.activationScripts.nerdNixosBuilderKey = { text = ...; }`
— the same custom-named-attribute pattern that nix-darwin silently
drops. Symptoms on bioskop:

* `/etc/nix/builder_ed25519` still contains the **old nix-darwin-auto-
  generated key** (for the embedded QEMU linux-builder), NOT the
  enriched `linux-builder` private from `/var/lib/ndh/ssh-keys/`.
* `nerd-nixos-builder: linux-builder key not yet deployed…` never
  appears in `/tmp/darwin-rebuild.log` (0 hits).
* Consequence: `ssh-ng://builder@linux-builder` falls back to the embedded
  QEMU builder; remote builds to `bioskop-nixos.lan` can't authenticate.
  `nix copy` from nerd-nixos bringup VM can't pull from the host store.

**Fix pattern** (same as nix-store-identity in commit 1a above): move
into `system.activationScripts.postActivation.text = lib.mkOrder <N>`
ordered after ssh-keys-enrichment (1500). 1600 is currently
nix-store-identity-deploy; consider 1650 or inlining the deploy into the
same block.

==== Secondary builder issue (separate)

`/tmp/tart-materialize.log` shows:

----
Failed to find a machine for remote build!
derivation: …-tart-nerd-nixos-materialize.drv
required (system, features): (aarch64-darwin, [])
1 available machines:
([aarch64-linux], 8, [benchmark, big-parallel, kvm, nixos-test], [])
----

The tart-nerd-nixos-materialize derivation is aarch64-darwin but the
only configured builder advertises aarch64-linux. Unrelated to the ssh-key
deploy, but worth noting: likely `buildMachines` needs a native Darwin
fallback, or the materialize derivation should declare
`preferLocalBuild = true`.

=== Cert principal "committed" still baked into signed certs

The `allPrincipals` lists in `modules/darwin/openssh.nix` and
`modules/nixos/openssh.nix` still include `"committed"`, and
`keys.yaml` still has `principals: { committed: committed }` entries.
Requires re-signing all certs + re-mapping — deferred as a separate
data migration.

== Suggested commit layout

. `fix(darwin): ssh-keys activation chain` — bundles 1a/1b/1c. All three
  are the direct fallout of running the bioskop switch end-to-end.
. `refactor(keys): rename profile role "host" → "system"` — bundles the
  schema + Nix + yq + shell + sops data changes. Mechanical rename,
  safe to land as one commit.
. `refactor(keys-validator): drop shadow, validate canonical` — small,
  shadow-file removal + flake validator retarget.

Can also fold (3) into (2) if you prefer — same topic, smaller PR surface.
